reasons: al-Kidd is a leading modern 'clearly established' qualified-immunity decision in the Harlow/Malley line: 'existing precedent must have placed the... question beyond debate' and QI 'protects all but the plainly incompetent or those who knowingly violate the law' (Malley).
'Key — Progeny / Refinement' on Qualified Immunity is well-grounded in the opinion's Part II-B.

reasons: Cached opinion: 'An arrest, of course, qualifies as a seizure of a person under this provision' — al-Kidd concerns a material-witness arrest/seizure, so a cross-doctrine link to Seizure of the Person is grounded.

Cached holding (star-verified pin-743): 'We hold that an objectively reasonable arrest and detention of a material witness pursuant to a validly obtained warrant cannot be challenged as unconstitutional on the basis of allegations that the arresting authority had an improper motive.'

Subjective-intent irrelevance: reasonableness 'is predominantly an objective inquiry... that action was reasonable whatever the subjective intent'; QI prong: 'Because Ashcroft did not violate clearly established law...' — every element of the asserted holding is confirmed.
Cached opinion: 'Justice Scalia... delivered the opinion of the Court' (majority; Kagan took no part) — 'Binding — SCOTUS' correct.
2011 SCOTUS opinion, never overruled; leading objective-reasonableness / 'clearly established' statement (cited approvingly in Mullenix, Messerschmidt per the treatment note).
